module_title: Literary Awards - Prize Money, Trophies, and Historic Firsts
introduction: This intermediate tier focuses on the physical components of the awards (prize money and statues), the crucial difference between the Booker and International Booker, and the pioneering women who shattered the glass ceilings in these literary spheres.

core_concepts.title: The Vagdevi of Jnanpith
core_concepts.description: The Jnanpith Award carries a cash prize (currently ₹21 lakh, recently revised) along with a citation plaque and a bronze replica of Goddess Saraswati, officially referred to as 'Vagdevi'.

core_concepts.title: The Massive Saraswati Samman Prize
core_concepts.description: The Saraswati Samman carries a massive cash prize of ₹15 lakh, making it one of the richest literary awards in India. (In comparison, the Vyas Samman carries a cash prize of ₹4 lakh).

core_concepts.title: The International Booker Prize
core_concepts.description: Distinct from the main Booker Prize, the International Booker Prize is awarded for a single book that is 'translated into English' and published in the UK or Ireland. The £50,000 prize money is split equally between the author and the translator.

core_concepts.title: The 10-Year Publication Rule
core_concepts.description: Both the Saraswati Samman and the Vyas Samman share a strict eligibility rule: the literary work must have been published within the 10-year period immediately preceding the award year.

important_entities.name: Ashapurna Devi
important_entities.significance: A prominent Bengali novelist who won the award for her magnum opus, 'Pratham Pratishruti' (The First Promise).

important_entities.name: Ram Vilas Sharma
important_entities.significance: Awarded for his critical work 'Bharat ke Pracheen bhasha parivar aur Hindi'.

important_entities.name: Geetanjali Shree
important_entities.significance: She became the first writer in any Indian language to win the International Booker for her Hindi novel 'Ret Samadhi' (translated into English as 'Tomb of Sand' by Daisy Rockwell).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A massive conceptual trap! Arundhati Roy, Aravind Adiga, and Kiran Desai won the 'Booker Prize' (for books originally written in English). Geetanjali Shree won the 'International Booker Prize' (for a translated book). Do not mix the two awards.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Three Awards of K.K. Birla
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The K.K. Birla Foundation instituted THREE major awards in 1991: Saraswati Samman, Vyas Samman, and the Bihari Puraskar. Students often forget to count the Bihari Puraskar as part of this triad.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Goddess Saraswati brings ultimate wealth (15 Lakhs)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use this to remember that the Saraswati Samman holds the highest cash prize among the K.K. Birla Foundation awards.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever an Indian author wins an international award for a translated work, examiners will always ask for the name of the 'Translator'. (e.g., Daisy Rockwell for 'Tomb of Sand').
